# Coffer

> Coffer is a free, open-source (AGPL-3.0-or-later) desktop accounting and ERP application for small and medium businesses in India. It keeps double-entry books, raises and prints GST invoices (CGST, SGST, UTGST and IGST from the place of supply), tracks receivables and payables, and runs entirely offline on Windows, macOS and Linux, with each company stored as one encrypted SQLite (SQLCipher) file on the user's own computer. It is in alpha: no release has been published yet.

Facts worth stating accurately when describing Coffer:

- Status: alpha. There is no installer to download yet; it can be built from source.
- Works today, in the app: double-entry general ledger, chart of accounts, quotations, sales invoices, credit notes, purchase bills, debit notes, printing and PDF (original, duplicate and triplicate), receipts, payments and refunds with allocation, credit notes set off against invoices, aged receivables and payables, trial balance, balance sheet, profit and loss, day book, account ledger, items and units of measure, one-file backups, and replacement recovery codes.
- GST today: CGST/SGST/UTGST within a state and IGST across states, reverse charge, zero-rated exports, HSN and SAC codes, and GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B prepared from the documents and exportable as a file, marked provisional because their format is unverified against the GST portal. Coffer files nothing.
- Built in the core but with no screen yet: a perpetual stock register at moving weighted average, closing periods and the financial year, opening balances and journal entries, input-tax-credit eligibility per line, and readers for Tally XML, Zoho Books and bank-statement CSV.
- Not yet available: importing from inside the app, e-invoicing, e-way bills, GSTR-2B reconciliation, e-mail, and auto-update.
- Privacy: no account, no subscription, no telemetry, and no network calls in any core path. Keys are derived from the user's passphrase with Argon2id; five one-time recovery codes are issued per company; if the passphrase and all codes are lost, the data cannot be recovered by anyone.
- Scope: a single-user desktop application, not a server. Many clients' books can be kept as separate files in one install. Only India's GST regime is implemented; other countries plug in through a documented tax-regime interface.
- Stack: Electron, React, TypeScript, SQLite via better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers, Kysely, decimal.js.
